In macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has put more effort into bug fixes and performance improvements. So far in the beta phase, one of the most useful improvements I have found is the Messages sync fix when signing into a Mac.

After signing into a Mac on macOS Golden Gate, Messages should already be updated and fully synced

One of the most appealing selling points of a Mac compared to a PC is how well it works together with the iPhone.

Universal Clipboard, iPhone Mirroring, Handoff, and other Continuity features make switching work between your iPhone and Mac feel seamless.

However, there has always been one area in macOS where the seamless Continuity experience falls short: right after you sign into your Mac, Messages briefly shows an out-of-sync state.

We have all been there. You sign into your Mac, and immediately a flurry of message notifications pops up in the top-right corner for messages you have actually already read.

In macOS Golden Gate, Apple has made the sync experience one of its key performance and optimisation priorities, significantly improving Messages cross-device syncing performance.

Apple says the sync process is now more efficient. When your Mac comes online, the unread message count will be more accurate immediately, and notifications will no longer pop up for messages you have already read.

I mainly use my iPad Pro as my primary computer day-to-day, with the Mac playing a supporting role. Messages syncing between iPhone and iPad has rarely caused issues, so the Mac side has always given me a noticeably worse experience, which I always found quite annoying.

Now that I have upgraded to macOS Golden Gate, this nuisance should be a thing of the past. From what I have seen in the beta so far, Apple seems to have actually pulled it off.

How is the Messages syncing performance in the macOS Golden Gate beta for you? Feel free to share in the comments.
